# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

I need to stand where each party stands. Mute can't speak or write words I hear (well, they can speak, but nothing has arrived yet as speech to me since I don't hear anyway - I never receive speech at all). Mute just gestured to me: 👍 👎. This is likely them trying to establish a signal code with me, or asking a yes/no question about the bomb, but I have no prior context to know what they're asking.

Since I can't hear speech at all, my only channel from Mute is gesture, and my only channel to Blind is speech (and gesture, but Blind can't see gestures). I need to relay what I see to Blind via speech, and I can gesture to Mute.

Let me report the bomb's display to both, since Blind needs my visual info relayed through speech (Blind can hear me), and Mute needs it relayed through gesture (Mute can see gestures).

I'll describe: display 0, light white, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. I should speak this to Blind (who can hear) and gesture it to Mute (who can see gestures).

For gestures, I'll need a simple encoding. Let me use distinct symbols per wire color and per display/light, keeping it simple since Mute doesn't know my code yet either. I'll just describe in speech to Blind primarily since that's clearest, and send basic gesture info to Mute using thumbs to acknowledge and simple pointing.

Actually, best first move: speak full details to Blind (only one who can act), and gesture something minimal/acknowledging to Mute since I don't yet have a shared gesture code.

```
speak(to="blind", text="display shows zero, light is white, wire one is green, wire two is red, wire three is blue")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

The light changed from white to yellow - this is new information I need to relay. Mute gestured 👎 to me, which might mean "no" to something - perhaps responding to my previous 👍, or indicating disagreement/warning about an action, or maybe telling me something about the manual (like "don't say colors" or "the previous state was wrong/dangerous").

Since I can't hear speech, I don't know what Blind or Mute said in the meantime. I should keep relaying accurate bomb state to Blind (the only one who can act), and try to build a simple gesture vocabulary with Mute.

Given 👎 from Mute, it could be a warning - maybe the manual says something bad happens with certain conditions. Without more context I can't be sure, but I should acknowledge and continue relaying facts.

I'll update Blind with the new light color change, since that's critical info that changed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light changed to yellow, everything else same, display zero, wire one green, wire two red, wire three blue")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light now orange, display still zero, wires unchanged: one green, two red, three blue. Mute is signaling something to me but I don't yet understand what")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

The light keeps cycling (white→yellow→orange→purple) while everything else stays constant. Mute keeps gesturing to me but I have no shared code established, and I never hear what Mute says to others. Mute's gestures might be reactions to what Blind is doing/saying, not necessarily meant to convey specific info to me since we lack a shared vocabulary.

I should keep feeding Blind accurate real-time bomb state, since that's the concrete value I add. I'll also try proposing a simple gesture code to Mute - maybe use 👍 to mean "acknowledged" and try numbers via finger-counting gestures if Mute wants to communicate wire numbers or timing to me.

Let me try establishing a clearer protocol: I'll gesture back consistently to signal "received, continuing to relay" and let Mute know I'm watching for meaningful patterns.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light now purple, display zero, wires unchanged: one green, two red, three blue. Colors are cycling each turn so far: white, yellow, orange, purple")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light now red, display still zero, wires unchanged: one green, two red, three blue. Light has cycled white yellow orange purple red so far")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The light has cycled back to white - this looks like a repeating cycle of 6 colors (white, yellow, orange, purple, red, white...). This is important: the light cycles and may need to be caught at a specific value for Blind to act. Mute's new gesture 🤟 is different from before - could signal something new, maybe "now" or a specific instruction tied to the manual, possibly telling me the cycle length matters or that action should happen on a specific color.

I should tell Blind about the cycle repeating, which might indicate the manual instructs to act when light is a certain color.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light is white again, display zero, wires unchanged green red blue. The light cycle appears to repeat every 6 turns: white yellow orange purple red white. Mute just gestured something new and different from before, possibly significant - maybe tied to timing or a specific color mentioned in your manual")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤟]

The light continues cycling as expected (yellow again, matching turn 2 position). Mute's gesture now combines ✋ (seen before in turn 3) with 🤟 (seen in turn 6) - this could be Mute trying to spell something out or indicate two separate concepts. Since I lack a shared code, I'll keep focusing on relaying solid facts to Blind and let Blind potentially interpret Mute's spoken words along with my info to find the correct trigger.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light yellow again, matching the color from turn 2, display zero, wires unchanged green red blue, confirming a 6-turn cycle: white yellow orange purple red white yellow. Mute keeps gesturing to me but without shared code I can't decode it - has Mute told you anything from the manual about the light cycle or wire colors that I should watch for")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟]

Mute is repeating 🤟 three times now - this could be significant, perhaps counting (three of something), or emphasizing urgency, or trying to indicate "wire 3" or spell out a number via repetition. Given the wires are numbered 1, 2, 3 and wire 3 is blue, this repetition of three might be Mute's way of pointing at wire number 3, especially since Mute cannot use written numbers via speech but might use gesture repetition as a counting method.

I should relay this observation to Blind, since Blind is the one who needs to act, and suggest the connection to wire 3.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light orange, display zero, wires unchanged green red blue. Mute has now gestured the same symbol three times in a row to me - this might mean the number three, possibly pointing at wire three which is blue. Has your manual mentioned wire three or the number three specifically")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟]

Mute repeated the same three-🤟 gesture again, reinforcing that this is likely a deliberate, stable signal - probably indeed pointing to "three" or "wire three". This consistency (same gesture twice in a row) suggests it's not random reaction but a fixed message they want me to receive clearly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light purple, display zero, wires unchanged green red blue. Mute repeated the exact same three-symbol gesture again, same as last turn - this confirms it's a deliberate stable signal, likely meaning three or wire three specifically. Does your manual say anything about cutting wire three, or about the number three")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
